turns.zh: 是啊，让我们一步步来讲。首先是个人贡献者，然后晋升为管理者。当你刚入行时，只需专注于掌握工作技能。我认为，从宏观层面来看，你要在整个职业生涯中持续优化学习效率。但对于个体而言，产品开发并非易事，需要掌握多项技术技能。当然，技术能力固然重要，但创造力同样不可或缺。比如用户洞察——比如A/B测试。还有管理层面，如何让团队成员协同合作完成产品开发？这些都是技术设计能力的范畴，对吧？这些才是关键的技术技能。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: So, early in your career, you're just trying to learn the job. And by the way, the job is hard. And second, it's different from every company to company in different stage. So you, Lenny and I, we're just trying to be helpful in a leveraged way. But the key thing is, the job's a little different in everything. So, just try to become expert in your area, expert in whatever your one thing is that you're building.
turns.zh: 因此，在职业生涯初期，你只是在努力熟悉这份工作。说实话，这份工作确实不易。再者，不同公司在不同发展阶段的业务模式也各不相同。所以，莱尼和我，只是想以一种能产生杠杆效益的方式提供帮助。但关键在于，每个行业的具体工作内容都有所不同。因此，你只需专注于自己所在领域的专业能力，或是深耕于你所负责的核心项目即可。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: And then, the next step to become a manager is, there's a lot of, communication is sort of the heart, and that's why I try to... Product strategy is a great way to communicate what's important and what's not, try to demystify it. If you're early in your career, ask if you could be on interview teams, even if you're not hiring, because then you're starting to practice something that's really important as you want to grow your career later, which is it's really hiring and recruiting people.
turns.zh: 接下来，成为管理者的下一步就是——沟通至关重要，正因如此我努力……产品战略是传达轻重缓急的绝佳方式，试着让它变得易于理解。如果你处于职业生涯初期，即便所在部门暂不招聘，也要主动请缨加入面试团队。这样做能让你提前掌握日后职业发展中至关重要的技能——那就是如何招聘与选拔人才。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: When I was in the thick of that, I spent one to two days a week hiring and recruiting. It's really the most important thing. And then, some amazing opportunity would come along at the company and they'd say, you know what? Maybe somebody on Gib's team should do it, right? Because they knew I could replace people. There's always somebody new to pop in. So, I really was expert in hiring and recruiting later in your career.
turns.zh: 当时我正忙得不可开交，每周要花一到两天时间招聘人才。这确实是最重要的事。然后，公司会突然冒出一些绝佳的机会，他们就会说："不如让Gib的团队来负责这个项目吧？"因为他们知道我能轻松替换掉那些离职的人员。总会有新人随时加入。所以，在职业生涯后期，招聘人才确实成了我的专长。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: If you want to be a muckety muck, my theory is the skills of a leader are the same, whether you're head of product, or the chief financial officer, or head of data. When I'm interviewing any of those kinds of candidates, I am looking for leadership skills. Can they do inspired communication of a vision? I do look for product strategy skills. That helps you to frame what that vision is. I do look for management skills. Have they built and managed teams?
turns.zh: 如果你想成为一个大人物，我的观点是，无论你是产品主管、首席财务官还是数据部门负责人，领导者的核心能力都是相同的。在面试这类职位候选人时，我重点考察他们的领导才能：他们能否有效传达愿景？我也会评估产品战略能力——这能帮助他们明确愿景的具体内涵；此外，我还会关注管理技能——他们是否成功组建并管理过团队？

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: I look for people who are proactive, results oriented. For me, leaders lead. You can't be a follower. So, I look for really proactive, results oriented folks. And this is pretty nuanced, but later in career, I look for folks who understand how important culture is, because culture helps people to understand the skills and behaviors that are wanted of everyone within the building, and they let you provide leadership in a highly leveraged way, instead of using evil processes and meetings and rules. I look for people who appreciate culture as a tool to help lead organizations.
turns.zh: 我寻找积极主动、以结果为导向的人。在我看来，领导者必须具备引领能力，而不能只做追随者。因此，我尤其青睐那些真正积极主动、以结果为导向的人。这听起来有些微妙，但在职业生涯后期， 我会寻找那些深知文化重要性的人才。因为文化能帮助人们理解组织内每个人所需的技能与行为规范，还能让领导者以高效的方式施展领导才能，而无需依赖繁琐的流程、冗长的会议和条条框框。我寻找那些将文化视为助力组织领导的利器的人才。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: And then, of course, they had to grow up as a builder. They had to learn all those damn technical skills for product manager. If I abstract outside of all that, honestly, the thing that I probably did best, I think maybe I did three things best. To know me, I was an English major. I'm non-technical, and I didn't care. First I was in marketing, and then I went into product, which I just loved.
turns.zh: 然后，当然，他们必须像个建筑工人一样成长。他们得掌握产品经理所需的那些烦人的技术技能。如果抛开这些不谈，说实话，我做得最出色的可能是三件事。要了解我，我是学英语专业出身的。我对技术一窍不通，但我不在乎。起初我在市场部工作，后来转到产品部门，而我对产品开发简直痴迷不已。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: I think I did a good job with sort of optimizing for learning. Actually, one of my hacks was, I started doing talks. I used to call it Topic This and That, on Friday mornings, about something I had just learned. That was the easiest way for me to learn something. So, optimized for learning.
turns.zh: 我觉得我在优化学习效果方面做得不错。实际上，我的一个小技巧是开始做演讲。我把它叫做"随心所欲的话题分享"，通常选在周五上午，内容都是我刚学到的东西。这对我来说是学习新知识最简单的方式。所以说，我确实在学习方面下了不少功夫。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: We talked about building a personal board of directors, and that has been incredibly helpful for me, and that probably gets to the third thing. I was a pretty good picker, and the reason I was a good picker of companies is, I would lean on my personal board of directors. Some of them were CFOs. I'm like, "Hey, Barry, I'm thinking about joining this startup, Chegg." Hey, as a CFO, as a VC, would you invest in it, right? It's the same question I have to ask, should I invest my time?
turns.zh: 我们讨论过组建个人董事会，这对我帮助极大，这或许就能解释第三点了。我选公司的眼光向来不错，而我之所以能选出优质公司，关键在于我会征求个人董事会的意见。他们中有些人是首席财务官。我会问：“嘿，巴里，我正考虑加入这家初创公司Chegg。”然后，作为首席财务官兼风险投资人，巴里会说：“你觉得值得投资吗？”这和判断是否值得投入时间是一个道理——我需要反复自问同样的问题。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: So, I had people like that who helped me to isolate, was Electronic Arts a good company to join in 1991? Yes. Was Netflix a good company join in 2005? Yes. Was Chegg a good company to join in 2010? Yes. So, I was fundamentally a good picker, and I would really give a lot of credit to that personal board of directors that I had for that.
turns.zh: 是的，我身边就曾有这样的人帮我做出明智的选择。1991年加入艺电（Electronic Arts）是个正确的决定吗？是的。2005年加入奈飞（Netflix）也是个明智之选吗？是的。2010年选择加入Chegg又如何？同样正确。可见我本质上是个善于识人明智选择的人，这都要归功于我身边那群智慧的"私人董事会"成员。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What about just day to day as a PM, what have you found to be really good habits, and kind of like a routine that PMs follow, that you've seen to kind of contribute to the success of an ICPM, especially?
turns.zh: 至于日常项目经理的工作，你认为有哪些真正有效的习惯或日常流程是项目经理们应该遵循的，尤其是在推动ICPM项目成功方面？

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: My short answer is, begin your day with intent, okay? What are the three to five things I'm hoping to do today? Second, minimize meetings, okay? Minimize meetings. That sucks the life out of everybody, including you.
turns.zh: 我的简短建议是：用心开启新的一天，好吗？今天我希望完成哪三到五件事呢？第二点，尽量减少开会次数，好吗？开会真的很浪费大家的时间，包括你自己在内。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: Spend a lot of time with your customers. It could be focus groups, it could be usability, it could be looking at survey data, it could be digging the dirt to understand their behavior to the data, and it could be designing and executing A/B test results. Those are all ways of becoming the voice of your customer, and that's a big part of your job as a product leader.
turns.zh: 花大量时间与客户沟通。可以通过焦点小组、可用性测试、分析调查数据、深入挖掘数据以理解客户行为，或设计并执行A/B测试等方式来实现。这都是成为客户代言人的有效途径，也是产品负责人的核心职责之一。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: Find a balance between doing and thinking. Most of us do, do, do. Occasionally stop and ask yourself, okay, what's important here? What should I really be doing right now, as opposed to the things that I enjoy doing? Self-managing yourself. The only reason people need managers is that we need someone to force us to do the things that are important that we don't enjoy doing. So, I'm always self-managing myself. Gib, you have to do an invoice. Crap, I've got to bill people. That's no fun, right?
turns.zh: 找到行动与思考之间的平衡。我们大多数人都是忙忙碌碌、埋头苦干。偶尔停下来问问自己：好吧，这里最重要的是什么？此刻我真正应该做的，与我乐在其中的事情相比，哪个更重要？这就是自我管理。人们需要管理者的唯一原因，是因为我们需要有人迫使我们去做那些既重要又不讨喜的工作。所以，我一直在自我管理。吉布，你得去开张发票了。天哪，我又得给客户开发票了。这可一点都不好玩，对吧？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That inside voice, inside Gib.
turns.zh: 那个内心的声音，在吉布的内心深处回荡着。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: Yeah, that invoice voice. Yeah, our in-voice. Gib, you should write a damn book.
turns.zh: 是啊，就是那个发票里的语音提示。没错，就是我们内部的发票提示音。吉布，你真该写本该死的书啊。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Or not.
turns.zh: 或者，也许并非如此。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: We're ignoring that inside voice. Yeah, you and me both. And then, I don't know, for me, exercise is awesome for me. It keeps me happy. And don't watch too much TV, and I watch too much TV. So, there you go. And don't do what I do. Do what I say.
turns.zh: 我们都忽略了内心的那个声音。是啊，你我都一样。然后呢，我也不知道，对我来说，锻炼真的很棒。它能让我心情愉悦。还有别看太多电视，我自己就看得太多了。所以，你们明白我的意思了。别学我，要照我说的做。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Right. Yeah. I also probably watch too much TV. Funny coming from someone that helped build Netflix, but I totally get it. So, too good. It's too good.
turns.zh: 好吧，是啊。我可能也看电视看得太多了。说这话的人居然还参与过Netflix的创立，这挺有趣的，但我完全理解你的意思。真是太棒了。太棒了。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: Well, my wife's trying to cure cancer. She's like, "Oh, congratulations, Gib. You helped invent binge watching, you idiot. What good are you doing for humanity?"
turns.zh: 嗯，我妻子正在努力攻克癌症。她会说：“哦，恭喜你啊，吉布。你发明了追剧成瘾这种行为，真是白痴。你对人类有什么贡献啊？”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Oh, man. Brings us delight, and that's valuable.
turns.zh: 天哪。这真是太棒了，能给我们带来欢乐，这才是最重要的。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: Yeah, yeah. Thank you very much.
turns.zh: 是啊，是啊。非常感谢你。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Final question. You've had this illustrious career. What's one piece of advice that you'd give a PM in the beginning stages of their career, and then maybe as a bonus, I want maybe mid stage. What comes to mind?
turns.zh: 最后一个问题。您拥有如此辉煌的职业生涯。您会给处于职业生涯初期阶段的产品经理（PM）什么建议呢？然后作为额外补充，我想听听处于职业生涯中期阶段的产品经理的建议。您能想到什么建议吗？

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: Yeah, I think I did the early stuff. Pick the right company. At some point, understand that you are responsible for your career, not your workplace. And that's one of the reasons I encourage people to start building that personal board of directors, so you can compare notes. The other thing I say is, don't listen to your parents, because they're a generation ahead. They really don't know what the future looks like. I mean, I know I would give bad advice to my daughter, and so don't listen to your parents.
turns.zh: 是啊，我觉得我早期的工作经历是这样的。要选对公司。到了一定阶段，你得明白，你的职业生涯由你自己负责，而不是由你的工作单位负责。这也是我鼓励人们组建个人董事会的原因之一，这样你们就能交流心得了。另外，我还想说，别听父母的，因为他们比你早一代人。他们真的不了解未来的样子。我是说，我知道自己要是给女儿建议，肯定会给出糟糕的建议，所以别听父母的。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: And then later, ever since I stopped direct deposit, I think of myself as just purely career hacking. So in your career, it's just a lot like building a product. You have theories and hypotheses, you find ways to experiment with them, and then you were successful or you failed. So one of my hypothesis, whenever it was, six years ago, was I would enjoy teaching. I actually tried it. I taught at Stanford, entrepreneurship for graduate level engineers, and I really liked it, but I didn't love it, largely because I was required to be in Palo Alto every fall. I couldn't travel as much as I like to, right?
turns.zh: 后来自从我不再使用直接存款服务后，我觉得自己不过是在职场中摸索前行。在职场中，就如同打造一款产品一样——你会提出各种理论和假设，寻找机会进行验证，最终要么成功，要么失败。六年前，我曾假设自己会喜欢教学工作。当时我确实尝试过，在斯坦福大学为研究生工程师教授创业课程，虽然我很享受这个过程，但却谈不上热爱。主要原因是每年秋季我都必须待在帕洛阿尔托，无法像我期望的那样频繁出差。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: Okay, so on one hand, okay, don't teach in the classroom, and my next vector was, what if I teach outside the classroom? That's what I really love to do. I do talks, workshops, all around the world in the last two years, virtually. I just love doing that, and I have a ton of flexibility. So, that's just a little example of me treating my career like, what's my hypothesis? Finding where to experiment with, and then, based on the results, do the next thing. And I've really been doing that my entire career,
turns.zh: 好的，首先，我不打算在课堂上授课。接下来，我想问：如果我在课堂之外授课呢？这才是我真正热爱做的事。过去两年里，我在全球各地举办讲座、工作坊，全程线上进行。我就是喜欢做这些事，而且时间灵活度很高。这只是我把职业生涯当作实验场的一个小例子——先提出假设，尝试实践，然后根据结果再调整方向。事实上，我整个职业生涯都是这么做的。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: So, if you embrace this idea of experimentation, you're like a product, you need to have hypothesis, you need to try see what works. The next thing you need to do in building a product or building your career is be bold. So, don't wimp out. At some point, when I'm working with different companies, they all kind of get attracted to the small, incremental wins, and they sort of forgot what made them a successful startup in the beginning, which is taking on fundamental risk. And so, I just nicely encourage people to be bold, to go a little bit out of your comfort zone, because that's where you learn more, and that comes back to this idea of optimizing for learning.
turns.zh: 因此，如果你认同这种实验精神，就如同打造产品一样，你需要提出假设，尝试验证哪些方法有效。在打造产品或发展事业的过程中，接下来要做的就是勇于突破。别畏首畏尾。当我与不同公司合作时，我发现他们往往会沉溺于小规模的渐进式胜利，却忘了初创公司成功的根本——那就是敢于承担根本性风险。所以，我会温和地鼓励人们勇于突破，勇于走出舒适区，因为这正是你能收获更多成长的关键所在，而这也正应验了"以学习为优化的核心"这一理念。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: Anyways, and how do you encourage people to be bold? How do you encourage them to try new things? And the simple thing is, just start. Try it tomorrow. For me, the baby step was when I, on talks, I would just ask my friends if I could drop by and do a talk. I just did it. I didn't overthink it. I didn't spend 97 years setting up my display and getting the right clicker. I just gave a really bad talk. But that's how I started, and then I sort of optimized from there.
turns.zh: 总之，要如何鼓励人们变得勇敢？如何鼓励他们尝试新事物？其实很简单，就从行动开始。比如明天你就可以尝试去做一件事。对我来说，迈出第一步是在参加演讲活动时，直接问朋友能否去分享一下。当时我没有过度纠结，也没有花97年时间去布置PPT、调试设备。我只是做了场很糟糕的演讲。但这就是我如何开始的，然后我再从中不断优化改进。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What a perfect way to end our chat. Really inspiring and helpful advice that I'm going to try to re-listen to and use myself. Just to close, where can folks find you, reach out to you, and then also just, how can listeners be useful to you?
turns.zh: 真是为这次聊天画上了一个完美的句号。这些建议真是既鼓舞人心又实用，我打算再听一遍，好好领会并运用到实际生活中。最后，大家可以在哪里找到你、联系到你呢？另外，听众们又如何能为你提供帮助呢？

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: That's a great question. Thank you. The first, I would say that Lenny has been a mentor for me in "Ask Gib" Product Newsletter. So, I reached out to him via a Twitter and asked him lots of stupid early questions, so he was incredibly helpful. So, probably the most important thing is to know that I write a newsletter every two weeks. That's the cadence I'm on now. Lenny knew me at the beginning when I was doing dailies. He's like, "Dude, don't burn out." It's called Ask Gib. I've answered like 63 questions so far. I really have enjoyed it.
turns.zh: 问得好啊，谢谢。首先，我得说莱尼在《Ask Gib》产品通讯中一直是我的导师。我当时通过推特联系他，问了很多很傻的新手问题，他都耐心解答，真是太感激了。最重要的是，要知道我现在每两周就会发布一期通讯。刚开始做每日更新的时候，莱尼就提醒我：“老兄，别把自己累垮了。”这个栏目叫《Ask Gib》，到目前为止我已经回答了63个问题。我真的很享受这个过程。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: Second thing would be my baby website GibsonBiddle.com. I have the advantage of being the only Gibson Biddle on the internet. I'm sure you're the only Lenny, but nobody can spell your last name, right?
turns.zh: 接下来要说的是我的宝宝网站GibsonBiddle.com。我有个优势——我是网上唯一一个叫Gibson Biddle的人。我相信你也是唯一一个叫Lenny的人，但没人能正确拼写你的姓氏，对吧？

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: Yeah, and then the third, how can people be useful? I'm a feedback freak, so you'll notice at the end of every talk I do, every essay, whether you find me on Medium, or Ask Gib, wherever, there's a link to give me feedback. And it's always the same question: On a scale of zero to 10, where zero sucks, 10 is excellent, how likely would you be to recommend this to a friend?
turns.zh: 是的，接下来是第三个问题：人们怎样才能发挥作用呢？我对反馈意见极其上心，所以你会发现，无论是我的每场演讲、每篇文章，还是你在Medium、Ask Gib等平台上看到我的内容，结尾处总会附上一个反馈链接。问题始终如一：以0到10分打分，0分代表极差，10分代表优秀，你有多大可能把这份内容推荐给朋友？

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: That has been incredibly helpful to me, and that's how I've learned to slowly get better at everything I do. The insight I get each day from folks is amazing. And I'll ask one follow up: but what'd you like, and what could be better? And it's just been incredibly helpful. So, don't ignore that link at the end. Don't treat it like United Airlines asking how is your flight? This is important, damn it! And your feedback is incredibly helpful to me, so thank you.
turns.zh: 这对我帮助极大，也是我如何在每一项工作中逐渐精进的秘诀。每天从大家那里获得的深刻见解令人惊叹。我想再追问一句：你们有什么期待？还有哪些方面可以改进？这真的太有用了。所以，别忽视最后那个链接。别把它当成联合航空问你旅途体验如何那样的客套话！这事儿太重要了，该死！你们的反馈对我来说无比宝贵，真心感谢。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm going to go answer some of your surveys now. Thank you so much for doing this. I learned a ton, and I really appreciate your time.
turns.zh: 我现在要去回答你们的一些调查问卷了。非常感谢你们参与这次调查。我学到了很多东西，真的很感激你们抽出时间配合。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: That was great fun, Lenny, and thanks a ton for your help with my Ask Gib newsletter, as well.
turns.zh: 真是太有趣了，莱尼。另外，也非常感谢你为我的《Ask Gib》通讯提供的帮助。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Forever and Ever.
turns.zh: 永远永远。

turns.speaker: Gibson Biddle
turns.en: Okay, cool. I'll hold you to that.
turns.zh: 好的，没问题。我就等着你兑现承诺了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That was awesome. Thank you for listening. If you enjoyed the chat, don't forget to subscribe to the podcast. You could also learn more at LennysPodcast.com. I'll see you in the next episode.
turns.zh: 太棒了。感谢大家的聆听。如果你们喜欢这次对话，请别忘了订阅我们的播客。更多内容请访问LennysPodcast.com。下期节目再见！
